supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-ACOLE-01 as sean.byrne with the command to execute \\FILE-ORC-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1, matching the organization's documented workstation-patching practice.
The PowerShell process used the same logon ID as a network logon by sean.byrne from WS-SBYRNE-01 shortly beforehand; the associated event records special privileges for that session.
PowerShell launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package, and both processes then exited, consistent with the stated business-hours patching activity.

The reported brief PowerShell appearance is temporally consistent with this observed, documented patching operation; the available evidence does not indicate that the alerted PowerShell execution was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process records show the script path and resulting update installer, but do not include the script contents or independently verify the contents of the remote share. (T284-00231, T284-00237)
The records establish process execution on the workstation, but do not establish what the user saw on screen or whether the reported window was specifically this process. (T284-00231, T284-00233)
claims_not_established: The exact contents and integrity of Patch-Workstations.ps1 are not established by the provided records.
The evidence does not establish whether Amy saw the PowerShell window she reported.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: WS-ACOLE-01 accessed Google Docs in Firefox, an unapproved cloud service under the provided inventory context. This activity occurred outside the alerted PowerShell execution. (T284-00041, T284-00042, T284-00061, T284-00062)

Separate ticket: WS-ACOLE-01 made a connection using the GoogleDriveFS user agent, and a Dropbox updater connection was observed; these indicate unapproved cloud-storage-related activity under the provided inventory context and are unrelated to the alerted PowerShell execution.
